security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, relative imports, safe local build scripts, or documentation that forbids risky patterns. Confirmed risks remain around broad all-site permissions, OpenAI network calls with page metadata, and client-side OpenAI API key handling. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Replace all-site HTTP and HTTPS matches with activeTab, optional host permissions, or a user-selected allowlist where possible.
Show a clear consent step, preview the data sent to OpenAI, minimize fields, and document the third-party transfer in privacy disclosures.
Prefer a backend proxy or short-lived scoped token. If direct keys remain, avoid echoing full keys and clearly warn users.
Update blueprint examples to lead with least-privilege permissions, explicit consent, and a backend-token option for AI requests.

semantic_findings.description: The manifest covers all HTTP and HTTPS pages, the content script collects page URL and SEO metadata, and the utility can send selected metadata to OpenAI. This data flow needs narrower permissions, clear consent, and privacy disclosure.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited code directly shows all-site coverage, page snapshot collection, and an external OpenAI POST. The action is user-triggered, but the privacy-impacting flow is clear.

semantic_findings.description: The background worker stores and retrieves the OpenAI API key from chrome.storage.session, and the popup loads the key into an input. Session storage reduces persistence, but the key remains exposed to extension code and UI.

content.value_statement: Chrome extension teams need safe Manifest V3 architecture, permissions, and review support. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through secure design, implementation, testing, and publishing tasks.
actual_capabilities: Plans Manifest V3 extension architecture across background, content, popup, offscreen, and shared modules.
Drafts permission and host permission strategies for Chrome extension manifests.
Guides secure AI API integration with consent, storage, and network boundary checks.
Produces TypeScript-oriented component guidance for messaging, scoring logic, and UI flows.
Creates security, privacy, performance, testing, and publishing checklists for extension reviews.
limitations: It provides guidance and code patterns, but it cannot guarantee Chrome Web Store approval.
It may require current Chrome policy verification before publishing.
It does not replace a full penetration test or legal privacy review.
The included sample uses broad host permissions that should be narrowed for production.

use_cases.title: Plan a New MV3 Extension
use_cases.description: Define components, permissions, data flows, and security checks before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Review an Existing Extension
use_cases.description: Audit manifest permissions, message flows, storage choices, AI calls, and publishing risks.

use_cases.title: Migrate MV2 to MV3
use_cases.description: Map background pages to service workers and update lifecycle, permissions, and testing plans.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a small extension
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Manifest V3 Chrome extension for this goal: [goal]. Include components, required permissions, data flow, and key security checks.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Component Guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the background worker, content script, popup, and shared contracts for this extension: [requirements]. Use TypeScript and least privilege.

prompt_templates.title: Review Security and Privacy
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Chrome extension design for security, privacy, permissions, CSP, storage, AI API calls, and Chrome Web Store disclosure risks: [design].

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Release Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a release readiness plan for this MV3 extension: [extension details]. Include tests, packaging checks, policy notes, and remediation priorities.

output_examples.input: Plan an AI SEO analyzer extension for the active tab.
output: Architecture separates page snapshot collection, background analysis, popup controls, and shared contracts.
Permissions include activeTab, storage, and only the host access needed for the chosen pages.
Privacy notes require user consent before sending page metadata to an AI provider.

output_examples.input: Review a manifest that runs on every website.
output: The review flags broad host coverage and recommends optional host permissions or activeTab injection.
It explains what data may be collected and where disclosure is needed.
It lists concrete changes before Chrome Web Store submission.

output_examples.input: Prepare a testing plan for a service worker extension.
output: The plan covers unit tests for shared logic, E2E flows for popup actions, and reload tests for worker lifecycle behavior.
It includes manual checks for permissions, consent, and network failure handling.

best_practices: Start with a data flow diagram before choosing permissions or storage.
Prefer activeTab, optional permissions, and explicit consent for sensitive page analysis.
Verify current Chrome Web Store policies before final packaging.
anti_patterns: Do not request all-site host access when a narrower permission model works.
Do not send page content to AI services without clear user consent and disclosure.
Do not store long-lived API keys in extension-controlled client storage when a token proxy is available.

faq.question: Does this skill build complete Chrome extensions?
faq.answer: It guides architecture, implementation, review, and release planning. The final code still needs project-specific validation.

faq.question: Does it support Manifest V3?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill focuses on Manifest V3 service workers, content scripts, popup UI, offscreen documents, and permissions.

faq.question: Can it help with AI API integration?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers AI request flows, consent, storage choices, and privacy review for external model calls.

faq.question: Can it guarantee Chrome Web Store approval?
faq.answer: No. It can prepare compliance checks, but current policy review and final submission remain required.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should teams review before production use?
faq.answer: Review host permissions, API key handling, consent language, network destinations, CSP, and test coverage.
